issues.description: In the solution, Genre.name is declared private (private let name: String) in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift, but Client (in Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift) accesses genre.name. In Swift, a private property is not accessible from other files, so this is a visibility mismatch that will cause a compilation error and confuse students. The problem statement describes Genre as having a String name (implying it should be readable for printing) but does not specify private visibility.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Genre.name property accessible from other files in the module by removing the private modifier (e.g. change 'private let name: String' to 'let name: String' or 'public let name: String' if module-wide public access is desired). This aligns the implementation with the problem description and allows Client to print genre.name without compilation errors.
